title: Uniform local minimality of the ball in the fixed-volume nonlocal perimeter problem among centered Lipschitz near-spherical sets
difficulty_reason: H3: a linear second-variation test at a ball does not supply a perturbation size that works uniformly as the kernels concentrate with epsilon. The author splits the full nonlinear nonlocal perimeter into a double-shell difference term and averaged ball perimeters, compares the induced spherical nonlocal seminorm with H1, and controls the perturbed rough-kernel contribution using k(r)=r|g-prime(r)|. The appendix constructs a two-variable coordinate map with an injectivity/Jacobian estimate and a near/far spherical decomposition, producing uniform perturbation bounds from the stated moments/tail hypotheses. Volume and barycenter identities remove the constant/translation harmonic modes; the local Fuglede estimate then combines with the nonlocal expansion to give the author coercive comparison and strict local minimum for(P_gamma,epsilon), with independent small t and epsilon thresholds. This uniform nonlinear rough-kernel/profile construction is the independent research-level core; planar convexification is not used. All printed rate/volume shorthand is retained with explicit source notes, without a correction or correctness certificate.
